questions.question: The difference between compound interest (compounding annually) and simple interest on a sum of Rs. 80,000 for 2 years is Rs. 288. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 80,000

Time (T) = 2 years

Difference between CI and SI = Rs. 288

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest (CI) = P(1 + r)T - P

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × T

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P × r²

**Calculation:**

Given: Difference between CI and SI = 288

We know, Difference = P × r²

⇒ 288 = 80,000 × r²

⇒ r² = 288 / 80,000

⇒ r² = 0.0036

⇒ r = √0.0036

⇒ r = 0.06 = 6%

**The rate of interest per annum is (6%).**

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on Rs. X at 7.5% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 22.50. Find the value of X.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest accrued on an amount of ₹40,000 in 2 years was ₹324. The rate of interest per annum was:
questions.solution:

**Calculation:-**

According to question-

⇒ P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ - 1] - (P × R × T)/100 = 324

⇒ 40000 [(1 + R/100)² - 1] - (40000 × R × 2)/100 = 324

⇒ 40000 [{(100 + R)²/100² - 1} - {R × 2}/100 = 324

⇒ 400 [{100² + R² + 2 × 100 × R -100²}/100 - 2R] = 324

⇒ [{R² + 200R}/100 - 2R] = 324/400

⇒ (R² + 200R - 200R)/100 = 324/400

⇒ R² = 32400/400

⇒ R² = 81 = 9%

∴** The rate of interest per annum is 9%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Formula used:-

Where,

questions.question: There is 70% increase in an amount in 7 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest on ₹8,000 after 3 years at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount increased by 70% in 7 years

For compound interest sum = Rs. 8000

Time = 3 years

**Concept used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

C.I = [P(1 + R/100)T - 1]

Here, P = sum, T = time, R = rate

**Calculation:**

Let the amount be Rs. 100a

So, increased amount = 100a + 100a × 70%

⇒ 170a

So, interest = 170a - 100a = 70a

Now, Let the rate of the interest be R

70a = (100a × 7 × R)/100

⇒ 7aR = 70a

⇒ R = 10

So, rate = 10%

Now, C.I = 8000[(1 + 10/100)³ - 1]

⇒ 8000[(1 + 1/10)3 - 1]

⇒ 8000[(11/10)3 - 1]

⇒ 8000[(1331/1000) - 1]

⇒ 8000[(1331 - 1000)/1000]

⇒ 8000[331/1000]

⇒ 8 × 331 = 2648

**∴ The compound interest is Rs. 2648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Simple interest is constant throughout the period.

So, 70% in 7 years = 10 % in 1 year

∴ R = 10% and T = 3 years

Let the sum be 10 units, So, Amount = 10 + 10/100 = 11

For three years , sum = 10³ = 1000

1000 units = Rs. 8000, therefore 1 unit = Rs. 8

And Amount = 11³ = 1331

Interest = 1331 - 1000 = 331

Interest = 331 × 8 = 2648.

∴ The compound interest is Rs. 2648.

questions.question: The difference between compound interest (compounding annually) and simple interest on a sum of Rs. 10,00,000 for 2 years is Rs. 2401. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:

Time (t) = 2 years

Difference between CI and SI = ₹2401

**Formula used:**

Difference = P × (r/100)²

**Calculations:**

2401 = 10,00,000 × (r/100)²

⇒ (2401 / 10,00,000) = (r/100)²

⇒ √(2401 / 1000000) = r/100

⇒ √2401 = 49 and √1000000 = 1000

⇒ (49 / 1000) = r/100

⇒ r = (49 × 100) / 1000 = 4.9

**∴ The rate of interest per annum is 4.9%.**

questions.question: A principal gets increased by 21% in 2 years at compound interest. What will be the simple interest on Rs. 1000 for 4 years at the same rate of interest?

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹80,000 at the same rate of interest per annum for 2 years is ₹98. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is calculated directly using the formula: Difference = P × (R / 100)²

⇒ 98 = 80000 × (R / 100)²

⇒ R² = (98 × 10000) ÷ 80000

⇒ R² = 98 ÷ 8 = 12.25

⇒ R = √12.25 = 3.5% = 3½%

**∴ The correct answer is 3½%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹80,000

Time (T) = 2 years

Difference between CI and SI (D) = ₹98

Let the rate of interest be R% per annum.

**Formula Used:**

Difference (D) = P × (R / 100)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64ff58be2778afee3f4d17ab0494effcd1a759a16d93e2f8c34f105c77a4a4fc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 98 = 80000 × (R / 100)²

⇒ 98 = 80000 × (R² / 10000)

⇒ 98 = 8 × R²

⇒ R² = 98 ÷ 8

⇒ R² = 49 ÷ 4

⇒ R = √(49 ÷ 4)

⇒ R = 7 ÷ 2

⇒ R = 3.5% or 3½%

**∴ The correct answer is 3½%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 3 years is calculated using the formula: D = P × (R / 100)² × (300 + R) ÷ 100.

Effective Rate for 2 years

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years at R% per annum is (2R + R² ÷ 100)%. The effective simple interest rate is 2R%. The difference is (R² ÷ 100)% of the principal.

Tree Method for Compound Interest

In the tree method, the second year's CI includes the interest on the principal plus the interest on the first year's interest. This interest on interest is exactly the difference between CI and SI for 2 years.
